before: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.
after: In the twelfth month the heir apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill. The heir apparent asked that he be made a prince, but the request was denied.

before: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Xian fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Xian but was not granted it.
after: In the twelfth month the Heir Apparent's eldest son Sima Bin fell ill; the Heir Apparent sought a princely title for Bin but was not granted it.

before: As Xian grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.
after: As Bin grew gravely ill, the heir apparent prayed and offered sacrifices on his behalf.

before: When Xian's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.
after: When Bin's illness grew grave, the Heir Apparent prayed and offered sacrifices to seek blessing for him.

before: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Marquis of Chewu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.
after: He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace. The heir apparent changed his garments, bowed twice, received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, and rode a rough ox-cart. Sima Dan, Duke of Dongwu, escorted him with armed guards, together with his consort Lady Wang and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang, to confinement at Jinyong.

before: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Marquis of Chewu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Xian, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.
after: Thereupon He Yu of the Masters of Writing and others were sent with credentials to the Eastern Palace to depose the Heir Apparent as commoner. The Heir Apparent changed his garments and came out, bowed twice and received the edict, walked out through the Chenghua Gate, rode a rough ox-cart, and the Duke of Dongwu, Sima Dan, with arms escorted the Heir Apparent, his consort Lady Wang, and his three sons Bin, Zang, and Shang together to be confined at Jinyong.

before: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Xian's mother, Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were executed.
after: The heir apparent's mother, Lady Xie the Gracious Lady, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were executed.

before: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Xian's mother, the Forest Keeper Jiang Jun, were killed.
after: The Heir Apparent's mother, the Gracious Lady Xie, and Bin's mother, Jiang Jun, a consort of baolin rank, were killed.

before: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Xian died.
after: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Bin died.

after: On the day bingzi the imperial grandson Bin died.

before: On guimao the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.
after: On guiwei the empress had Cheng Ju, Director of Imperial Physicians, prepare poison.

before: On the day guimao Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.
after: On the day guiwei Empress Jia had the Director of Imperial Physicians Cheng Ju compound poison.

after: An edict ordered arrest of the Jia clan; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and Eight Seats were summoned at night.

before: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.
after: An edict ordered the Masters of Writing to arrest the Jia kin; the Secretariat Supervisor, attendants, Yellow Gate Gentlemen, and the Eight Seats were all summoned into the hall at night.

before: Xiu became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.
after: Xiu became Secretariat Director; power radiated from him; the realm served Xiu, not Lun.

before: Xiu was Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.
after: Xiu was Secretariat Director; his authority shook the court; the realm served Xiu and sought nothing from Lun.

before: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Xian as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.
after: An edict restored Yu's title, sent He Yu to bring the coffin from Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Bin as Prince of Nanyang and brothers Zang and Shang as princes.

before: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Xian as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Xian's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.
after: An edict restored the former Heir Apparent Yu's title and rank, sent the Masters of Writing He Yu leading Eastern Palace officials to meet the Heir Apparent's coffin at Xuchang, posthumously enfeoffed Yu's son Bin as Prince of Nanyang, and enfeoffed Bin's brothers Zang as Prince of Linhuai and Shang as Prince of Xiangyang.

before: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."
after: Lun's staff hid behind trees, each tree studded with hundreds of arrows. From chen to wei, Chen Huai, Secretariat Director and Hui's elder brother, wished to aid Yun and told the emperor: "Send the white tiger banner to stop the fighting."

before: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."
after: Lun's staff all hid behind trees to stand; each tree received hundreds of arrows. From the hour chen to wei, the Secretariat Director Chen Huai—Hui's elder brother—wished to support Yun and said to the emperor: "The white tiger banner should be sent to halt the fighting."
